title: The Border
timelinePosition: Story start. No prior chapter. Midday-to-afternoon patrol; the mage crossed the first ward ring before dawn.
openLocation: Southeastern Eversong Woods, on Farstrider patrol near the Amani frontier
transport: Thalassian horses for Sylvanas, Lor'themar, and the mounted patrol
immediateObjective: Finish the troll sweep, dodge the Convocation budget session, and stay outdoors one more day.
constraints: Limited third on Sylvanas only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, or infer.

Jaina is 'the mage', 'the human', or 'the prisoner' in Sylvanas's head for the whole chapter, including after Cyndia says the name in Beat 8. The name exists in Cyndia's dialogue only; Sylvanas's narration never switches to 'Jaina'.
Jaina does not speak on-page. No Jaina dialogue before the chapter boundary.
No trust, warmth, or partnership behavior between Sylvanas and Jaina.
The word 'plague' does not appear in any thought or speech. Leylines are an unverified claim relayed second-hand, not a known fact.
No physical manifestation of the magical danger on the page. Ward-stone malfunction is report, not demonstration.
No proof that this is more than a human trespass.
Silvermoon is never cut to. Convocation pressure is felt through Lor'themar and Sylvanas's avoidance.
Pre-undeath Sylvanas: dry, exact, tactical interior. No banshee theatrics, no confessional emotion-naming.
Scene 3 closes on the outline's locked demand; chapter 2 must not replay it.

The name 'Jaina Proudmoore' has to come from somewhere that is not Jaina talking. Cyndia's identification comes out of the impounded gear, worked out after the runner had left the post (so Beat 4's 'identity unknown' and Scene 3's 'no verified identity' both stay true). Sylvanas checks it against the Farstrider watch-file she already carries in her head. Which object in the gear gives it away is the writer's call.
Ward geography: the mage crossed the first ring and was taken at the second. Beat 4 (runner) and Beat 7 (Cyndia) must agree on this.

Ward-stone hum and pulse on the ride (Beats 3 and 6) is the normal living border grid, getting denser toward the Pass. It is not an anomaly and it is not a sign of the danger. The only sign that something is wrong with the stones is Cyndia's report in Beat 7.

povKnowsAtOpen: Routine Amani pressure exists on the southeastern frontier.
The ward network looks stable in every formal report.
The Farstriders keep files on powerful human mages near the border.
Jaina Proudmoore is one of the names worth watching.
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: That a human mage has already crossed the ward boundary.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: Any trust between Sylvanas and Jaina.
Proof that this is more than a human trespass.
Real proof the magic warning is legitimate.
A physical manifestation of the magical danger.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Jaina is in Farstrider custody and has to make her case directly to Sylvanas.
Sylvanas knows the prisoner is Jaina Proudmoore, Antonidas's apprentice, not a random trespasser.
The breach has turned from patrol annoyance into a serious interrogation.
Sylvanas does not know why Jaina is here, whether Antonidas knows, or whether the warning is true.

pov: She opens treating anything south of the wards as someone else's problem unless it touches her stones, roads, or riders.
She wants to finish the troll work, stay on her horse, and avoid the Convocation budget session.
The report of a human mage inside the wards turns an easy patrol day into her problem.
By the end, the border mess belongs to her, and the prisoner is waiting in her own holding space.

beats: Before Sylvanas sees her, Jaina is just the human mage who ruined an easy day.
Sylvanas expects a polished Kirin Tor problem: spy, diplomat, or both.
What she finds instead is a road-worn young mage who looks exhausted, furious, and very far from court.
Even then, Jaina is still only the mage, the human, or the prisoner inside Sylvanas's head.

team.label: Partnership
beats: There is no partnership here. One woman is in custody, and the other decides how hard the door stays shut.
Jaina shifts from paperwork headache to the one person Sylvanas has to hear out.
The chapter ends on their first hard face-to-face with no warmth and no softening.

castAndHandoffRules: Lor'themar Theron: present in Scenes 1 and 2. Exits north in Scene 2 to brief the Convocation.
Mounted patrol: present in Scenes 1 and 2. Leaves north with Lor'themar once the report lands.
Ranger Cyndia: enters in Scene 3 as the border-post officer. Remains active into Chapter 2.
Farstrider runner: Scene 2 only. Delivers the report, then rides back south with Sylvanas to the post.
Jaina Proudmoore: seen in Scene 3, but does not speak on-page in this chapter.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 2 opens at Cyndia's post on the interrogation beat. Lor'themar and the mounted patrol are already northbound; Sylvanas, Jaina, and Cyndia inherit the scene.

scene.title: The Prisoner
scene.sceneFunction: A generic border arrest becomes a high-stakes problem that locks both women into the next chapter.
scene.knowledgeAtSceneStart: A human mage is in a holding cell. No verified identity. No trusted warning. Sylvanas has only the runner's thin report and a rapid ride behind her.

beats.goal: Get the raw facts of the arrest from Cyndia and decide what to do with them.
beats.conflict: The facts make the mage stranger rather than clearer: she did not bolt, she argued to stay and work; the stones are misreading in ways nobody can place.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas gets the whole account but not an answer, and decides the report is odd enough to see the prisoner now.

newOnPageInformation: The mage arrived before dawn and reached the second ring.
She did not bolt; she argued to stay and work.
The ward-stones read as if malfunctioning from something inside them (Cyndia's report, not demonstrated on page).
Her staff and gear are in lockdown.
The prisoner's name does not come up in this beat.
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether she is arrogant, terrified, or correct.
beats.transitionIntent: planted-question: the account is too strange to judge at second hand. She goes to the door.
beats.plannerWarning: Beat 4 and Beat 7 are both report beats. Beat 7 must not replay the runner's account; it should add the second ring, the argument to stay, the stones' behavior, and the gear lockdown. The outline's 'ward-stones malfunctioning' stays Cyndia's reported observation to respect 'do not add: physical manifestation'.
beats.arcLanding: POV bullet 4 starts here: the prisoner is in her own holding space.

beats.goal: Size up the prisoner and confirm what kind of problem this is.
beats.conflict: The person in the chair does not match the polished Kirin Tor type she expected, and nothing about the scene gives her an easy label.

outcome.summary: The prisoner is Jaina Proudmoore, Antonidas's apprentice, and the incident has just become diplomatic and magical, not just a trespass.

newOnPageInformation: The prisoner is a young mage in practical travel gear, worn boots, frost-burned knuckles, ink stains.
Her fury that nobody believes her shows in her body and how she holds herself. She does not speak.
Cyndia gives the name: Jaina Proudmoore, Antonidas's apprentice. It comes from the impounded gear, and Sylvanas checks it against the Farstrider watch-file. Jaina's own speech is not the source.
Her staff stands on the weapons rack, in sight and out of reach. That is what the lockdown looks like.
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Why Antonidas let her walk out alone.
Whether Antonidas knows where she is.
beats.transitionIntent: emotional-carryover: the name turns her irritation into a temper the stakes no longer allow. Beat 9 opens with her pushing it down.
beats.plannerWarning: Name source gap: Jaina does not speak on-page and the outline says 'no verified identity' at scene start, yet Cyndia names her. Needs an in-world source that is not Jaina's dialogue, e.g. identification found among her lockdown gear (Kirin Tor sigil, letters) or an earlier off-page statement relayed by Cyndia. Left to writer/verifier; planner adds no new on-page object beyond the gear already in lockdown.
beats.arcLanding: Jaina-through-POV bullets 3 and 4: road-worn, exhausted, furious, nowhere near court, and still 'the mage' in Sylvanas's head after the name is spoken.

beats.emotion: Temper shoved down; anger turned to cold assessment.
beats.dilemma: Letting the trespasser wait and stew, or putting her out are both worse than hearing her now; interrogating without any reason to trust her is its own risk.
beats.decision: She stops weighing options and goes straight to interrogation, opening with a flat demand that she start talking.
newOnPageInformation: Releasing the trespasser is off the table.
Stalling the interrogation is judged as risky as releasing her.
Sylvanas chooses to hear Jaina out herself, with no warmth.
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether Jaina is telling the truth.
beats.transitionIntent: planted-question (chapter close): the outline's locked demand hands the interrogation to Chapter 2. Chapter 2 opens on the answer and does not replay the line.
beats.plannerWarning: Closing line is a locked outline demand ('Start talking'). Plan treats it as locked content and the only Sylvanas line fixed in advance. Chapter 2 must not replay it.
beats.arcLanding: POV bullet 4 (the border mess is hers). Partnership bullets 1 to 3: custody, the one person she has to hear out, and a face-to-face with no warmth.

factsLocked: They inherit Jaina after she has stewed in detention for hours.
Sylvanas walks in already knowing Jaina's identity; it does not need explaining in Chapter 2.
Jaina has not delivered her plague/leyline warning on the page.
The final demand at the close of Beat 9 caps this chapter; Jaina's POV in Chapter 2 does not replay it.
factsNotEarned: Real proof that the magic warning is legitimate.
Any trust, warmth, or partnership behavior between Sylvanas and Jaina.
A physical manifestation of the magical danger on the page.
